sections.h2: Which offices touch a deed in Marion County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Three county offices handle every Marion County deed, always in the same sequence: engineer, auditor, recorder. The recorder comes last and is the one that places the deed in the permanent public record. You can reach the recorder at 740-223-4100, the auditor at 740-223-4020 and the engineer at 740-223-4110.

Beyond deeds, the recorder files mortgages, easements and related land papers. An online records system lets anyone look up property documents. Paper copies and certified copies are another matter, since the recorder says they require a visit in person or a written request with payment enclosed. The system's own disclaimer tells users to read the actual document, because database entries can be changed without notice.

sections.h2: What does each office do with the deed?
sections.html:
The county's published instructions give the order, which differs from counties that send the deed to the auditor first.

  • Engineer. Staff compare the deed's legal description with the engineer's records and stamp it approved. That stamp expires after 60 days, so a deed left sitting must be stamped again.
  • Auditor. The seller completes and signs a conveyance form. Payment has to arrive before processing begins, and the auditor then stamps the deed as transferred.
  • Recorder. The office confirms the deed was signed and acknowledged correctly and carries both earlier stamps. After recording, the original is kept for imaging and data entry and then mailed back or picked up.

Several other papers follow the same route: a certificate of transfer, an affidavit of survivor, a life estate, a transfer on death designation and a land contract. Putting the engineer first means a faulty description is caught before any money is paid to the auditor.

sections.h2: How much do the engineer, auditor and recorder charge?
sections.html:
Fees come from two places. The auditor's conveyance charge is a local rate, and the recorder's charge follows state law. A notice on the recorder's home page says Senate Bill 94 added $5.00 to recording fees for most documents starting January 1, 2025.

Marion County deed steps and rates, quoted from the county's pages
OfficeWhat the county states
EngineerApproval stamp on the legal description, valid 60 days
Auditor, conveyance$4.00 per $1,000 of the sale price
Auditor, line fee50 cents per parcel in the transfer
Auditor, very small sale$4.00 minimum conveyance fee plus line fees under a $1,000 price
Recorder$34.00 covers two pages, $8.00 each later page (rate dated October 17, 2019)

The auditor's online fee calculator asks for the total price, rounded up to the next dollar, and the parcel count. A box marks transfers that qualify as exempt on state form DTE 100 EX. Let the auditor confirm the final total before you write a check.

sections.h2: Can I send a Marion County deed through the mail?
sections.html:
You can, provided the stamps come first. The recorder's page states that, since September 1, 2005, no deed is accepted by mail unless it already bears current engineer and auditor stamps. The county describes three mailings:

  • The deed alone goes to the engineer, with a stamped, self-addressed return envelope
  • The approved deed then goes to the auditor with a signed conveyance form, a check and another return envelope
  • The twice-stamped deed finishes at the recorder with the recording fee

Expect the recorder to take about five days. That window covers proofing, imaging, and a side-by-side comparison of the image against the original before the deed goes back in the envelope you provided. Electronic filing skips the mail altogether. The recorder lists four companies: CSC at 855-200-1150, ePN at 888-325-3365, Simplifile at 800-460-5657 and Indecomm at 651-765-6400.

sections.h2: Can the recorder's closed days change a closing date?
sections.html:
They can. The recorder publishes a closure list that goes beyond the usual holidays. The 2026 version named Good Friday, Juneteenth, part of July 2 and all of July 3, and the afternoon of September 10 plus all of September 11, when the office closed for the Popcorn Festival because of parking. It also showed closings for Veterans Day, most of Thanksgiving week, the afternoon of December 11, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, and New Year's Day 2027.

A deed cannot be recorded on a closed day. A buyer's lender sometimes wants proof of recording before releasing funds, so ask the title company which date it plans to file, and plan around the office calendar when the target falls near a holiday.

sections.h2: What does Marion County look like for homeowners?
sections.html:
Marion County lies in the middle of Ohio, bordered by Crawford, Morrow, Delaware, Union, Hardin and Wyandot counties. It was erected on February 20, 1820, reorganized in 1824, and named for Francis Marion, a South Carolina officer in the Revolutionary War. At 404 square miles it ranks fifth-smallest in the state. The city of Marion holds the seat and the largest population, and U.S. 23 joins state routes 4, 37, 95 and 309 among its main roads.

QuickFacts from the Census Bureau paint a modest market:

  • 2020 headcount of 65,359, with an estimate of 65,115 for 2025
  • Owners live in 67.5 percent of occupied homes
  • Typical owned-home value for 2020 to 2024: $156,800
  • Typical monthly gross rent: $864
  • Typical household income: $59,371
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree: 14.7 percent

Of 27,348 housing units in 2020, 8.8 percent stood empty, and about two of every three residents lived in an urban area. Only 60 building permits were issued in 2025, so existing houses make up most of the sales.

sections.h2: What else does the recorder publish for property owners?
sections.html:
The home page carries two warnings, a property fraud alert and a notary fraud alert, each linking to details. The Documents and Forms page holds three items: a public records policy, security procedures for electronic recording, and a notice to Medicaid Estate Recovery of a pending transfer of property by transfer on death deed.

That last notice concerns transfer on death deeds. Ask the office whether it applies before you plan a transfer of that kind. Staff cannot give legal advice and say some questions may need an in-person visit, so bring the deed and any prior recording references.

sections.h2: How do property taxes fit into a Marion County sale?
sections.html:
Call the County Treasurer at 740-223-4030, the office that takes every property tax payment. According to the auditor, the rate on a bill is the sum of voted levies and bond issues, and Ohio limits unvoted taxation to 10 mills, which works out to $10 per $1,000 of assessed value. Whatever exceeds that was approved by county voters.

The auditor's property search site accepts payments: look up the parcel by number, owner or address, open the tax tab on the property record, and add the amount due to your online cart, where you can adjust it before checkout. Debit and credit cards incur a 2.5 percent fee with a $1.50 floor, e-checks cost a flat $1.50 up to $10,000, and the page shows the amount before you submit. For a seller, the practical step is to request a balance from the treasurer ahead of closing, so the title company can pay anything owed out of the proceeds and the buyer receives a clean record.

faqs.q: What number reaches the Marion County Recorder?
faqs.a: 740-223-4100. The engineer's line is 740-223-4110 and the auditor's is 740-223-4020.

faqs.q: How many days does the engineer's stamp last?
faqs.a: Sixty. A deed that waits longer needs a fresh stamp before the auditor and recorder will take it.

faqs.q: What does the Marion County auditor charge on a sale?
faqs.a: The county prints $4.00 per $1,000 of sale price plus 50 cents per parcel. A non-exempt sale under $1,000 pays a $4.00 minimum plus the line fee.

faqs.q: How quickly does the recorder send a deed back?
faqs.a: That time covers proofing and imaging.

faqs.q: Is electronic recording available in Marion County?
faqs.a: Yes. The recorder names CSC, ePN, Simplifile and Indecomm as e-filing companies you can contact.
